entries.summary: Therapy is the day-to-day care that is resolved through the patient's Disease Recovery roll, including how many patients a physician can handle and how subordinates share his Prognosis. The Prognosis Total must be recalculated if apothecary or chirurgeon help is lost or the disease changes Severity.
quotes: Recovery Modifiers + Magical Aid + stress die
A physician can provide therapy to a number of patients at a time equal to his Medicine Ability

entries.title: Prevention of Disease (Regimens)
entries.summary: A physician can set a patient on a regimen that improves the patient's Living Conditions Modifier after a year, with the size of the bonus limited by the physician's Medicine and the number of clients. The bonus is lost if eucrasia is disrupted and takes a year to re-establish.
quotes: Clients = Physician's (Medicine x 5) Bonus to Living Conditions Modifier: +1 Minimum Medicine: 1
Single Client Bonus to Living Conditions Modifier: +3 Minimum Medicine: 7
Each physician can only manage a single regimen

entries.title: Regimens and Covenants
entries.summary: Gives the multiplier applied to Inhabitant points when covenfolk are kept on a regimen, making the diet expensive for the covenant's finances.
quotes: Increased to +2 | x2
A regimen cannot be instituted if the covenant is applying Emergency Savings to their food budget

entries.title: Treatment of Wounds
entries.summary: Expands the core Wound Recovery roll by splitting the Chirurgy bonus into a First Aid bonus and a Palliative Care bonus.
quotes: Stamina + First Aid Bonus + Palliative Care Bonus + Recovery Modifiers + Magical Aid + stress die

entries.title: First Aid
entries.summary: First aid given within a day of injury adds a bonus to Wound Recovery, and a successful First Aid roll can also let a patient act as though his wounds were one category less serious for a day.
quotes: First Aid Bonus to Wound Recovery: (Chirurgy / 2)
First Aid Roll: Dexterity + Chirurgy + Recovery Modifiers + Magical Aid + stress die vs Improvement Ease Factor

entries.title: Palliative Care
entries.summary: Ongoing wound care adds a bonus to Wound Recovery; the combined Chirurgy bonus from first aid and palliative care is capped by the Chirurgy of the caregiver. Also covers how many patients can be cared for and how subordinates help.
quotes: Palliative Care Bonus to Wound Recovery: (Chirurgy / 2)
cannot exceed the Chirurgy Ability of the character supplying the palliative care

entries.title: Specialties for Chirurgy
entries.summary: Lists the areas of practice that suit as specialties of the Chirurgy Ability under these rules.
quotes: the following areas are suitable as specialties in the Chirurgy Ability: surgery, surgical intervention, first aid, palliative care, midwifery

entries.title: Chirurgical Magic
entries.summary: Explains how Creo Corpus can duplicate the benefits of first aid and childbirth help, and how Rego Corpus can mimic surgery using an Intelligence + Finesse roll against the mundane Ease Factor plus a modifier.
quotes: Intelligence + Finesse roll against an Ease Factor equal to (Ease Factor for the mundane surgeon + 3)
Magical surgery involves no cutting

entries.title: New Creo Corpus Guidelines (Chirurgical)
entries.summary: Spell guidelines for treating wounds as less serious for activity purposes and for granting bonuses to childbirth rolls.
quotes: The target's wounds are treated as one category less serious for the purposes of activities while injured
Give a character a +6 to childbirth rolls

entries.title: New Rego Corpus Guidelines (Surgery)
entries.summary: Spell guidelines for performing magical surgical procedures of graded severity, which inflict or prevent worsening of wounds of matching category.
quotes: Perform a trivial surgical procedure (inflicting a fatigue level)
Perform a life-saving surgical procedure, preventing an Incapacitating or Fatal Wound from worsening

entries.title: Surgery
entries.summary: Rules and table of Ease Factors for surgical procedures, each of which inflicts a wound on the patient but gives a bonus to the next Disease Recovery roll on success. Failure and botch results are described.
quotes: Dexterity + Chirurgy + Recovery Modifiers + stress die
the patient receives a +3 to his next Disease Recovery roll
Phlebotomy, cautery, and cupping can only affect the most trivial diseases (Severity 5 or less) on their own

entries.title: Nurses
entries.summary: Describes how a nurse can lead or assist in first aid, palliative care and, with some Medicine, therapy.
quotes: a nurse can act as the lead chirurgeon in both first aid and palliative care

entries.title: Surgical Intervention
entries.summary: When a Wound Recovery roll fails, a chirurgeon can attempt emergency surgery to stop the wound worsening, at the price of a permanent consequence that depends on the wound's severity. A failed or botched Surgery roll makes matters worse, and lists give the Flaws and Characteristics affected by the wound's location.
quotes: He must make a Surgery roll (see Surgery, above) against an Ease Factor of 9
Make an immediate Aging roll
Gain a Major Flaw appropriate to the type of wound

entries.title: Midwifery
entries.summary: Rules for resolving childbirth in play by treating labor as a pseudo-wound to the mother, with consequences for the baby as her condition changes.
quotes: The onset of labor is treated as a Medium Wound to the mother, except that Wound Recovery rolls are made every 2 hours
suffers a –2 penalty to his Chirurgy Ability

entries.title: The Practice of the Apothecary
entries.summary: Explains how Profession: Apothecary complements Medicine, and how a physician's constant access to an apothecary reduces the Disease Recovery penalty for lacking medicinals.
quotes: is reduced by the Profession: Apothecary Ability, although it cannot become a bonus
Profession: Apothecary is an adjunct to Medicine

entries.title: Commonly Used Ingredients
entries.summary: A table of common medicinal ingredients with their qualities and ruling planet, which can supply Shape and Material Bonuses for magi and philosophers according to their strongest degree.
quotes: Use the largest degree of hot, cold, moist, or dry as the strength of the bonus.

entries.title: Medicinals
entries.summary: Defines the four degrees of strength of a medicinal and what each does to the body, and describes the effects of heating, moistening, drying and cooling medicines.
quotes: causes destruction or death of tissue
Medicinals of the fourth degree are all poisonous

entries.title: Pharmacy
entries.summary: Describes forms of medicinal preparation and gives a Dexterity + Profession: Apothecary roll, with an Ease Factor by duration, to determine how long a preserved ingredient keeps. Preservation can also extend the Duration of an Arcane Connection that is a plant or animal part.
quotes: Make an Dexterity + Profession: Apothecary roll
the Duration of the Arcane Connection is increased by one category
Only Arcane Connections that are plants or animal body parts can be extended in this manner by an apothecary

entries.title: Poisons
entries.summary: Fourth-degree substances act as poisons, with different effects for each quality. Poison manufacture falls under Profession: Apothecary, and only simple poisons can be made without knowing the correct formula.
quotes: Only simple poisons (those that inflict a Light Wound, and that have an Ease Factor of 6 or less to resist the damage

entries.title: The Apothecary's Store
entries.summary: An apothecary generates Labor Points each season he practises his trade, loses stock every year and through extra drains such as regimens, formulae and ligatures, and can avoid those drains by searching for specific ingredients with a stress roll modified by terrain, season and assistants.
quotes: Labor Points per Eligible Season: (Intelligence + Profession: Apothecary) x Wealth Multiplier
An apothecary's business loses 36 labor points every year
Per + Profession: Apothecary, against Ease Factor of 9

related.text: City & Guild Chapter Two: Labor, pp.37-40

entries.title: Pharmacy Magic
entries.summary: How Creo, Intellego and Rego Craft magic can stock an apothecary's store, speed the search for ingredients, or duplicate the preparation of ingredients.
quotes: then the Ease Factor of searching for ingredients is reduced by 3
such spells require an Intelligence + Finesse roll equal to the Ease Factor + 6

groups.title: Travel
groups.intro: Travel by land and sea, ships, navigation and their dangers.

entries.title: Travel
entries.summary: Guidelines for daily travel distances on foot, mounted, by cart and at sea, and the Long-Term Fatigue cost of hurried travel.
quotes: Attempts to travel quickly cost one Long-Term Fatigue level per day, as long as the characters actually travel.

entries.title: Guides and Messengers
entries.summary: Grogs plan journeys by itinerary and local knowledge, use Area Lore for navigation, and a successful Area Lore roll when planning a long journey can cut the travel time.
quotes: The Area Lore Ability is used for all sorts of navigation rolls
Intelligence + Area Lore roll of Ease Factor 12

entries.title: Travel Speeds
entries.summary: How far characters travel in a day on foot, horseback, by cart, coach or ship, including forced marches that cost Long-Term Fatigue, the effect of Athletics and Ride, changing horses, and how encumbrance and cross-country travel reduce distance.
quotes: 15 + (2 x Athletics) on good roads
30 + (2 x Ride) on good roads

entries.title: Travel Fatigue
entries.summary: Table of typical miles per day by mode of transport, with and without taking Long-Term Fatigue.

entries.title: Purchasing Supplies for Travel
entries.summary: Where and when grogs can buy food while traveling, with example prices and a rule of thumb for what it costs to feed a grog for a day.
quotes: Broadly speaking, it costs a Mythic Penny to feed a grog for a day, if you are buying rather than growing his food.

entries.title: Arranging Accommodation
entries.summary: Finding lodging in remote places uses a Communication + Folk Ken roll against an Ease Factor set by the kind of accommodation, with The Gift's social penalty applying if the peasants have talked with the magi.
quotes: make a Communication + Folk Ken roll, using the Ease Factors in the following table

entries.title: Means of Transport (relative costs of sea, river and road)
entries.summary: Compares the cost and speed of sea, river and road travel, which the rest of the chapter uses for planning journeys and cargo.
quotes: River travel is about twice as expensive as sea travel

entries.title: Vessels and Cargo Capacity
entries.summary: Defines the tun as the unit of cargo capacity used for all vessels, land and water.
quotes: a ton of cargo takes up as much space and carrying capacity as a tun

entries.title: Land Vessels (pack animals and carts)
entries.summary: Load capacities, costs, road requirements and crew needs for pack animals and carts.
quotes: A single person can effectively lead and tend three pack beasts if walking with a halter to the first beast, or six if riding.

entries.title: River Barges
entries.summary: Capacity and crew of river barges and lighters, which vary with the depth of the water.
quotes: Optimally, they have three crewmembers, but many have only a man and a boy.

entries.title: Seagoing Ships (buss, cog, galley, nef)
entries.summary: Describes the main seagoing ship types with typical cargo capacity, crew and cost, including limits on ship size and the larger crews of southern lateen-rigged ships.
quotes: A sailing ship costs four pounds per ten tons of cargo it can carry.

entries.title: Comparison of Traveling Speeds
entries.summary: Gives ranges of miles per day for river barges, road cargoes, riders, coaches, couriers and sailing ships, in standard miles.
quotes: Sailing vessels travel roughly 60 to 80 miles per day.
River barges travel 8 to 10 miles per day, faster downriver than upriver.

entries.title: Comparison of Traveling Costs
entries.summary: Passage prices and relative costs for sea, river and road travel, chartering a ship, the surcharge for known magi, and the profit a carrier typically keeps.
quotes: River travel costs twice as much as sea travel.
Known magi may need to offer double their usual fee for passage

entries.title: Ship Combat
entries.summary: Overview of how ships fight: boarding and cramped melee are usual, with artillery, ramming and oar-shearing as alternatives.

entries.title: Softening the Enemy (artillery, ramming, shearing oars)
entries.summary: Rules for shipboard artillery kills, galley ramming resolved by opposed captain rolls, and shearing oars to incapacitate rowers.
quotes: Two captains compare rolls of (stress die + Intelligence + Profession + up to 3 for experienced crews)

entries.title: Boarding and Melee
entries.summary: Captains' opposed rolls decide whether a predator boards or a victim escapes, followed by group combat with a height bonus for merchant ships and extra crew from sacrificed cargo space.
quotes: the two captains compare rolls of (stress die + Intelligence + Profession + up to 3 for experienced crews)
The added height grants them a +3 bonus on Attack and Defense Totals until they are boarded.

entries.title: Sea Monsters (attacks on ships)
entries.summary: How creatures of different Size threaten a ship: small ones barely harm it, while large ones hit automatically and destroy it as an environmental effect over rounds chosen by the storyguide.
quotes: Ships are so large that melee attacks against them automatically hit, and missile weapons have a +6 attack bonus.

entries.title: Adding Places to the Land Trade Map and Naval Trade Tables
entries.summary: A procedure for working out travel times to new places by dividing direct distance by a set figure for road, river with or against the current, or sea, plus a note on standard versus nautical miles.
quotes: Divide that distance by 12 for road travel.
For sea travel, divide the direct distance by 60.

entries.title: Naval Trade Tables
entries.summary: Sidebar tables of sea travel times between ports in six regions, joined by junctions; a voyage is planned by adding the times to each junction and then to the final port.
quotes: A player designing a voyage simply adds together the times to each junction, then to the final port.

groups.title: Mass combat and sieges
groups.intro: Battles between armies, heroic deeds in them, and sieges.

entries.title: Medieval Armies
entries.summary: The categories of troops in an army, the Living Conditions and disease cost of campaigning, the usual mix of units, and the baggage units an army needs, with a Leadership penalty when they are missing.
quotes: Characters suffer a –1 Living Conditions modifier for each year during which they spend at least one season in a campaigning army.
For every ten units in an army (rounded up) the army also needs one unit of baggage.

related.text: Art & Academe p.46 Disease Avoidance Roll

entries.title: Vassals
entries.summary: A table of the standard combat groups of each troop type a lord can raise from his household and vassals by rank, how losses are replaced, and the use of scutage.
quotes: the table below shows the average number of standard combat groups (each consisting of five fully equipped men)

entries.title: Mercenary Budget
entries.summary: How much a noble can spend on mercenaries by rank and wealth without lowering his standard of living, the Allied Troops Table, mercenary unit costs, and how a character may borrow against his income for a larger budget.
quotes: A character who is Poor may not do this.
A character who is average may become Poor and in exchange borrow five times the average mercenary budget of someone of his class in coin.

related.text: Covenants Chapter Five (cost of an armed force)

entries.title: Mercenary Units
entries.summary: A table of the cost in Mythic Pounds and experience level of typical mercenary combat groups.
quotes: The table below lists the costs of typical mercenary combat groups.

entries.title: Allies
entries.requires: An ally or agent from a Virtue or story event
entries.summary: A character with an ally or agent may claim that ally's forces, with the troupe's approval.
quotes: may claim the forces of that ally or agent, with the approval of the troupe.

entries.title: Affinity
entries.summary: A regional leader calls lesser nobles to his banner with a roll whose result multiplies his core vassal force, using the Allied Troops Table.
quotes: Presence + Leadership + Affinity score simple roll

entries.title: The Articles of War
entries.summary: The Church's Peace of God and Truce of God, which protect certain people and forbid fighting on certain days, and the sin of breaking them or executing prisoners.
quotes: The Truce of God (Treuga Dei) restricts the days on which war can be waged.

entries.title: Chevauchee
entries.summary: A scorched-earth raiding tactic, with a Living Conditions penalty to the Aging rolls of those who return to the ravaged land and a possible Infernal aura in extreme cases.
quotes: Those returning to such an area suffer a –2 Living Conditions modifier (in addition to any existing modifiers) to their next Aging roll.

related.text: Realms of Power: The Infernal pp.11, 15

entries.title: Allied Troops Table
entries.summary: Converts the result of the affinity roll into a proportion of extra allied forces, with a list of situational modifiers to the roll.
quotes: a character must roll better than 12 to raise additional allied forces past his own core force.

entries.title: Winning the Battle from Afar
entries.summary: When the player characters are not central to a battle, the storyguide simply decides its outcome from the needs of the wider story and the characters' actions.
quotes: the storyguide should simply decide the outcome of the battle

entries.title: Crusaders
entries.summary: How the Church raises an army to crusade, using the Senior Clergy character's Holy Influence roll against an Army Size Table.
quotes: is treated as having an affinity equal to the most prominent noble within his diocese or see

related.text: Realms of Power: The Divine pp.38, 93

entries.title: Heroic Endeavors
entries.summary: The overall approach to playing a battle as a series of vignettes with a player character as the decisive force, using the standard or optional combat rules.
quotes: Battles are played as a series of vignettes, each with a player character as the decisive force.

related.text: LoM Chapter Nine: Optional Combat Rules

entries.title: Territorial Advantage
entries.summary: Each army generates a Deployment Total, and the difference gives territorial advantage; commanders may delegate the roll to a lieutenant, and the battlefield's features and auras affect events.
quotes: Deployment Total: Intelligence + Area Lore + Stress Die
Territorial Advantage: Deployment Total – Enemy Deployment Total

related.text: Realms of Power: The Infernal p.10

entries.title: The Flow of Battle
entries.summary: The four-step sequence for running a battle: territorial advantage, weight of numbers, a battlefield event for each player character, and deciding victory.
quotes: The Weight of Numbers modifier is determined and assigned.

entries.title: Weight of Numbers
entries.summary: A bonus or penalty to event totals from the ratio of army sizes counted in standard combat groups, recalculated as losses mount.
quotes: The size of an army is measured in standard combat groups of five individuals.

entries.title: Battlefield Events
entries.summary: How a battle is broken into pivotal events, each with a Battle Ease Factor that rises as the battle goes on, which the focal character must meet with an Event Total built from an Event Bonus of Maneuver, Enemy and Size.
quotes: Event Total: Stamina + Leadership + Territorial Advantage + Weight of Numbers Bonus + Event Bonus
Event Bonus: Maneuver + Enemy + Size
Unless otherwise stated, each battlefield event lasts five combat rounds.

entries.title: Maneuver
entries.summary: The kinds of action a battlefield event demands, each with an Event Bonus value and win conditions: Defend, Attack, Run the Gauntlet, Take and Heroic Gesture.
quotes: If the leading character dies during a Heroic Gesture, the event is won and the player should describe how that death secures victory.

entries.title: Size
entries.summary: How many opposing combat groups a battlefield event involves, each option with an Event Bonus value, and how Weight of Numbers changes group sizes.
quotes: The Size of a battlefield event describes the number of combat groups the characters must defeat before they can win the event.

entries.title: Enemy
entries.summary: The kind of opponents in a battlefield event, from levies to special foes to attacking the baggage, each with an Event Bonus value; attacking baggage costs Reputation.
quotes: Characters choosing this Enemy option gain 1 experience point towards a bad Reputation.

entries.title: Wounds and Attrition
entries.summary: Losses to the defeated side after each event, the losing commander's Morale roll and rally attempt, and how player characters can rally a failing army.
quotes: the commander of the losing side must make a Morale roll (see Chapter Nine: Optional Combat Rules) against Ease Factor 6.
On a failure, the commander can attempt to rally his forces (Ease Factor 9) at the beginning of the next event.

related.text: LoM Chapter Nine: Optional Combat Rules (Morale)

entries.title: Example Battlefield Events
entries.summary: Worked examples of battlefield events, each showing the Maneuver, Size and Enemy chosen, the resulting Event Bonus and how the event plays out.
quotes: Each round in which a light wound is inflicted on them prevents them advancing, otherwise they advance 15 paces each round.

entries.title: The Aftermath of Battle
entries.summary: Rewards of victory in Confidence Points and Reputation, treatment of the wounded and their ability to travel, and the fate of prisoners by rank.
quotes: A successful battle earns the victorious characters one Confidence Point for each successful battlefield event whether they took part in that event or not.
The leader of the army also gains 1 experience point towards an appropriate Reputation.

entries.title: Standard Combat Groups
entries.summary: Combat statistics for standard five-person groups of knights, serjeants, infantry, archers, levies and baggage, and which are trained or untrained.
quotes: Each group is assumed to be five individuals.
a group that serves together for a season is treated as trained thereafter

entries.title: Knights Banneret and Mercenary Captains
entries.requires: Knight Banneret or Mercenary Captain status
entries.summary: These characters always treat their company as one combat group regardless of weight of numbers modifiers.
quotes: always treat their company as a single combat group regardless of any Weight of Numbers modifiers.

entries.title: Using Magic to Seize Advantage
entries.requires: Magic affecting terrain or troop deployment
entries.summary: Spells that alter terrain or misdirect troops add to the friendly Deployment Total.
quotes: Add the highest magnitude of any spell used to affect the terrain, or the deployment of troops, to the friendly side's Deployment Total.

entries.title: Mercenary Troops
entries.summary: Specialist mercenary troops may differ from the standard unit statistics, and a historical example of daily pay for knights, serjeants and infantry.
quotes: Richard's knights received one shilling per day while his mounted serjeants received four pence per day

entries.title: Siegecraft
entries.summary: Introduces the abstract siege rules, which resolve the capture and defense of castles and fortified towns through military events rather than negotiation, and leaves the final fall of a castle to troupe judgment.
quotes: It is for the troupe to determine when a castle finally becomes indefensible.

entries.title: Magic on the Battlefield
entries.summary: Sets the Concentration rolls needed to cast spells amid a battle and explains how the Group and Boundary targets can be scaled up to affect units or battlefield areas.
quotes: Concentration roll against an Ease Factor of 9 in order to cast spells
Boosting the spell level by one magnitude increases the diameter to around 300 paces.

entries.title: Example Battle
entries.summary: A worked example of resolving a battle through a series of battlefield events, showing how the lead character's total, the Weight of Numbers modifier, the Ease Factor and the Event Bonus fit together.
quotes: He needs an Event Bonus of +2 to reach the Ease Factor.

entries.title: Describing Castles
entries.summary: Introduces the three characteristics (Garrison, Defenses, Supplies) that describe a castle for siege play, each with a quality and a check interval.
quotes: the lowest interval pertaining to a given castle determines how often key siege events are played out when the castle is besieged

entries.title: Castle Garrison
entries.summary: A castle's Garrison is rated by the number of combat groups in it, which sets both the check interval and the Weight of Numbers modifier used in siege rolls.
quotes: The castle Garrison is measured in combat groups

entries.title: Castle Defenses
entries.summary: Rates a castle's walls and earthworks by quality grade to give a Defense Bonus and check interval, and uses castle size to work out how many damage levels each of its four walls has.
quotes: Permanent defensive enchantments also add +1 to the overall Defense Bonus.
The castle's Defense Bonus is multiplied by the damage level modifier from the above table to determine the castle's damage levels.

entries.title: Castle Supplies
entries.summary: Rates the food and materials stored in a castle and its ability to resupply, giving a check interval and a Siege Conditions Bonus used when the castle is stockaded.
quotes: Supplies include the food, water, and raw materials stored inside the castle, and the ability of the castle to resupply itself.

entries.title: Life Under Siege
entries.summary: Explains what happens when a siege begins, how besieged castles and cities handle their populations, and the Living Conditions penalty for characters who spend a season under siege.
quotes: Characters under siege suffer from a –2 Living Conditions modifier each year in which at least one season is spent under siege.

entries.title: Stockade
entries.summary: Rules for starving out a castle: the besiegers must cover enough walls, and at each check interval the castle makes a supplies roll whose failure degrades its supplies and can bring disease or surrender.
quotes: Supplies Roll: Siege Conditions Bonus + stress die
Ease Factor: 3 + Garrison Weight of Numbers Modifiers + Number of Years Under Siege

entries.title: Making Supply Rolls
entries.summary: A shortcut for resolving a long siege quickly by rolling several supplies dice in one batch instead of one roll per interval.
quotes: roll four dice to quickly resolve the passing of a month

entries.title: Laying Siege
entries.summary: Describes how a siege is played as a series of decisive events at intervals set by the castle's weakest characteristic, and the attacking and defending options available to each side.
quotes: There are three options: undermining the walls, launching an artillery assault, or scaling the defenses.

entries.title: Siege Engines
entries.summary: Statistics table for ballistae, mangonels and trebuchets (initiative, attack, damage, crew, range, cost), with notes on reloading and how they are used against walls or troops.
quotes: Reloading these weapons takes two minutes and requires the whole crew.

entries.title: Troop Deployment
entries.summary: Each army designates units as miners, artillery or soldiers and assigns them among the four castle walls; an undefended wall may provoke an undefended escalade.
quotes: each army may nominate any number of its units as miners, artillery, or soldiers

entries.title: Undermining
entries.summary: Siege event in which miners tunnel under a chosen wall and burn the supports; attacker and castle each roll Intelligence plus Profession Sapper, and success lowers the castle's Defense Quality.
quotes: Mine Attack Total: Intelligence + Profession Sapper + Stress Die
Castle Defense: Intelligence + Profession Sapper + Defense Bonus + Stress Die
If the Mine Attack Total exceeds the Castle Defense, the mine attack is successful.

entries.title: Artillery
entries.summary: Siege event in which groups of mangonels and trebuchets batter walls; a successful attack inflicts damage levels on the wall, and a wall reduced to nothing no longer gives the castle its Defense Bonus there.
quotes: Artillery Attack: Intelligence + Siege Weapon Ability + Engine Attack Bonus + Stress Die
Castle Defense: Intelligence + Profession Siege Engineer + Defense Bonus + Stress Die

entries.title: Escalade
entries.summary: Siege event in which attackers scale the walls, resolved with the battlefield event rules with modifications for garrison, defense bonus and wall breaches.
quotes: Each victory by the attacking side reduces the castle's garrison characteristic by one step (beginning with the next siege event).

entries.title: Option: External Defenses
entries.summary: Optional rule letting a castle have outlying fortifications, bought as an extra minor castle, that attackers must capture first; they have their own Defense Bonus but share the main castle's supplies and garrison.
quotes: Such features have their own Defense Bonus but rely on the larger castle's supplies and garrison.

entries.title: Escalade Weapons and Defenses
entries.summary: Describes siege towers, ladders, cats and battering rams for attackers and incendiaries for defenders, and how to treat rams and boiling liquids with existing weapon and damage rules.
quotes: Battering rams are treated as bludgeons.

entries.title: Counterattack
entries.summary: The garrison may sally out to destroy specific enemy units, or fire its own siege engines at the enemy's engines; sorties are resolved as events with a fixed Battle Ease Factor and no Territorial Advantage or Weight of Numbers.
quotes: These actions have a Battle Ease Factor of 9.

entries.title: Example Siege Events
entries.summary: Three sample siege events (Scale the Ladders, Open the Gates, Take the Marshal), each with an Event Bonus built from the Man, Size and Enemy modifiers, showing how to frame a siege scene for a player character.
quotes: Event Bonus +7
(+2 Run the Gauntlet, +4 I Stand Alone, +2 Expensive)

entries.title: Castle Free Choices
entries.requires: Virtue: Landed Noble or Great Noble
entries.summary: Lists the simple strongholds (island, manor house, ringwork, small tower) a Landed or Great Noble can pick for free, with a description of how each works defensively.
quotes: may select any of these options to describe his stronghold without spending extra money annually

entries.title: Minor Castles
entries.requires: Virtue: Landed Noble or Great Noble
entries.summary: Describes the shell keep and tower keep castle options for Landed or Great Nobles, with the yearly upkeep paid out of the character's frivolous spending money and the cost of extra guards.
quotes: must pay two pounds per year
at the rate of one pound per man per year for mediocre servants

entries.title: Curtain Walls and Mural Towers
entries.summary: Describes great castles with curtain walls and mural towers, their yearly maintenance cost, the extra infantry required as guards, and the political cost of building many towers.
quotes: A castle costs five pounds a year to maintain

entries.title: Keep Alternatives for Castles with Curtain Walls
entries.summary: Options for the keep of a curtain-walled castle (hall keep, courtyard castle, gatehouse keep) plus what a barbican and moat represent in game terms and how they affect upkeep.
quotes: A barbican and moat are included in the cost of a castle with curtain walls.
A moat has no upkeep fee; it's a free choice for characters with castles that have curtain walls.

entries.title: General Situational Modifiers
entries.summary: Guidance for assigning bonuses to Attack or Defense for battlefield circumstances, suggesting the values +1, +3 and +6 as slight, substantial and very significant edges, and phrasing modifiers as applying to the character in the unusual situation.
quotes: it is often easiest to simply choose between +1, +3, and +6

entries.title: Cover
entries.summary: Cover that actually stops attacks grants a Defense bonus against missile and melee attacks according to how much of the body is covered; it does not stack with concealment, only the higher bonus applies.
quotes: The Defense bonus from cover applies against both missile and melee attacks.
If a character has both cover and concealment, only the highest Defense bonus applies.

entries.title: Concealment, Darkness, and Invisibility
entries.summary: A table of concealment levels giving melee Attack and Defense bonuses (or Evasion) to hard-to-see characters, applying to both sides, plus extra botch dice for poor visibility and a pointer to the detailed invisibility rules.
quotes: These bonuses and penalties apply to both the attacker and the defender.

related.text: Houses of Hermes: Societates pp.32-33 Invisibility in combat

entries.title: Higher Ground
entries.summary: Fighting from an elevated position gives a small Attack and Defense bonus against lower opponents, but mounted characters already include height in their mounted bonus unless charging down a steep slope.
quotes: he enjoys an advantage that often translates to a +1 bonus to Attack and Defense in both melee and missile combat against opponents lower than himself

entries.title: Light Sources and Range of Visibility
entries.summary: Table giving the longest range at which each level of concealment applies in conditions such as moonlight, torchlight, rain and fog, with an optional Perception roll to reduce the concealment by a step.
quotes: a Perception roll of 9+ can sometimes reduce (by one step) the level of concealment due to poor visibility

entries.title: Fighting Indoors and in Narrow Spaces
entries.summary: Limits how many opponents can attack a defender in confined spaces such as against a wall or in a corridor, and notes cover, concealment and a penalty for large weapons in cramped quarters.
quotes: A character with his back to a wall can be attacked only by four opponents at once.

groups.title: Tournaments
groups.intro: Jousts, the melee and the life of the tournament.

entries.title: The Tournament
entries.summary: Overview of how a tournament unfolds from the commencailles and regars through the estor, melee and prize feast.

entries.title: Rules of Melee
entries.summary: The customs of a tournament melee: safe territory, protection of non-participants, points of honor, and how knights break the rules.

entries.title: Ransom
entries.summary: How surrender and ransom work in a melee, what may reasonably be demanded from knights of different means, and the Reputation cost of failing to pay.
quotes: Those who do not make good their promises gain 1 experience point towards an appropriate negative Reputation.
Service cannot be demanded as a ransom, nor can oaths of loyalty.

entries.title: Companies of Men
entries.summary: Knights fight in companies acting as trained groups, who may try to isolate a target and grapple the rider to lead him off for ransom.
quotes: Companies engage as trained groups of usually no more than ten individuals (or six if using the core combat rules)
A grappled rider loses control of his horse to his attackers.

entries.title: Tournament Combat
entries.summary: Melee fighting uses the optional non-lethal combat rules, which characters may drop round by round, and special maneuvers from the optional combat chapter may be used.
quotes: Botches in non-lethal combat almost always inflict real damage to one party or another.

related.text: LoM Chapter Nine: Optional Combat Rules, Option: Non-Lethal Combat

entries.title: Jousting
entries.summary: How a joust is resolved: each charge is one combat round using the optional shock of the charge rules, with botches possibly breaking equipment or injuring horse or rider.
quotes: Each charge comprises a single combat round

related.text: LoM Chapter Nine: Optional Combat Rules, Option: Shock of the Charge

entries.title: Melee Events Table
entries.summary: A random-encounter table for the tournament melee, rolled with Prudhomme Reputation as a modifier, that says what kind of opponent presents itself and carries growing botch dice for each event rolled.
quotes: Rolls on this table have a modifier equal to the character's Prudhomme Reputation.
Botch dice on the roll are equal to 1 + (1 per melee event rolled so far).

entries.title: The Grand Charge
entries.summary: The first of two ways to play the tournament melee: a series of stress rolls on the Melee Events Table giving chances to claim ransom, with opponents accumulating wounds as the melee goes on.
quotes: characters in the melee make a stress roll on the Melee Events Table.
assume that the opponent(s) have picked up a new short-term light wound

entries.title: Gaining and Losing Reputation
entries.summary: Lists tourney achievements and the experience points each earns towards Prudhomme Reputation in a season, taking the highest reward earned.
quotes: Extracting ransom from a stronger opponent earns 2 experience points.

entries.title: Staging a Tournament
entries.summary: How often tournaments of different sizes occur and when in the year they are held.
quotes: a large tournament — in excess of a thousand knights — can be found on average once per season

entries.title: Bohorts, Tirocinia, and Jousts
entries.summary: Defines the informal bohort, the youth-only tirocinium and the joust as variants of the tournament, and points to the non-lethal combat rules for the bohort.
quotes: Use the non-lethal combat rules on ArM5, page 174

related.text: LoM Chapter Nine: Optional Combat Rules, Option: Non-Lethal Combat

entries.title: Costs
entries.summary: What a patron spends to host a tournament, the quality of prizes, and a rule of thumb for how much he should spend relative to his Prudhomme Reputation.
quotes: a patron should spend ten Mythic Pounds per point of his Prudhomme Reputation to hold a tournament.

related.text: City & Guild p.69 superior quality works

entries.title: Team Sponsors
entries.summary: The cost to a sponsor of retaining knights to fight under his banner at tournaments.
quotes: Most nobles can expect to pay four Mythic Pounds per season per knight retained for tourney.

entries.title: High Ambition
entries.requires: Characters wishing to influence the whole melee
entries.summary: Runs the melee as a massed combat with custom story events, applying a short list of modifications to the massed combat rules.
quotes: There is no territorial advantage or weight of numbers bonus.

entries.title: Company Reputations
entries.summary: Deeds done under a company banner build a Reputation for the company itself, usable only by knights who ride in its colors.
quotes: Companies have a Reputation named after its leader or chant, which applies only within the tournament circuit.

entries.title: Patronage
entries.summary: Experience points toward Prudhomme Reputation earned by hosting tournaments and by commissioning an artist to record them, shared among co-hosts.
quotes: Hosting one or more tournaments in a season earns 1 experience point, or 2 if the event is particularly lavish.

entries.title: Tournaments as Income
entries.requires: Errant knight living off the tournament circuit
entries.summary: Applies the Labor Points system to knights who earn a living by tourneying, with seasons needed per year depending on wealth, plus guidelines for extra Labor Points from stories.
quotes: It costs 36 Labor Points per year for an errant knight to sustain himself.
The knight gains Dexterity + Single/Great Weapon Labor Points per season on the tourney circuit.

entries.title: Awards
entries.summary: Guidance for storyguides on how prizes are won at a tournament and how valuable a prize should be.
quotes: Storyguides should consider one Mythic Pound per point of Prudhomme Reputation as a baseline.

gated.title: Schools of magical combat
gated.intro: House Flambeau's schools of fighting with magic.

entries.title: Enhancing Spell Penetration
entries.summary: Practical advice for overcoming high Magic Resistance: favor low-level spells, improve Penetration, use Spell Mastery, and add Arcane and sympathetic connections.
quotes: so if one has both a name and a picture of one's target, the multiplier would be x4

related.text: ArM5 p.84 Arcane and sympathetic connections

entries.title: Schools of Magical Combat
entries.summary: Introduces the Flambeau idea of a 'school' of magical combat: a named, coherent style combining particular Arts, Abilities and spells.

entries.title: Choosing a School
entries.summary: How magi pick a combat school to suit their Hermetic Virtues and Flaws, and how Flambeau apprentices have a school chosen for them by their parens.

entries.title: Schools of Magical Combat at a Glance
entries.summary: Quick-reference table of the six example schools, what each does, and the Virtue recommended for it.
quotes: | The Founder | Attacks using fire | Puissant Ignem |

entries.title: The School of the Founder
entries.summary: Fire-based combat school: strengths, weaknesses and play advice for a magus who relies on Ignem attacks.
quotes: Ignem spells do excellent damage compared to other spells of similar magnitude.

related.text: ArM5 p.87 Spell Mastery magic resistance

entries.title: The School of Apromor
entries.summary: Perdo-based combat school aimed at damaging opponents directly, with versatile non-damaging uses but heavy demands on Penetration and Spell Mastery.
quotes: Perdo spells usually disregard the target's Soak

entries.title: The School of Boreas
entries.summary: Combat school built on the single combination of Perdo Ignem, using cold and darkness; a narrower, cheaper-to-learn alternative to the Apromor and Founder styles.
quotes: The School of Boreas relies on the single Form-Technique combination of Perdo Ignem.

entries.title: The School of Ramius
entries.summary: Combat school that bypasses Magic Resistance with mundane weapons backed by defensive magic, including the problem of a magus's own Parma Magica blocking self-targeted spells.
quotes: Spells of Personal Range always bypass the caster's own Magic Resistance (ArM5, page 85), but Touch- and Voice-Range spells are resisted.

entries.title: The Schools of Sebastian
entries.summary: A family of minor combat schools that conjure harmful substances with Forms other than Ignem, usually supported by a Magical Focus.
quotes: Most members of the Sebastian family of schools have a Magical Focus (either Major or Minor)

entries.title: Magical Foci for the Schools of Sebastian
entries.summary: Sample Magical Foci by Form suited to the Sebastian schools, with note on which count as Major.
quotes: Except where noted, all of them would count as Minor Magical Foci.

entries.title: The School of Vilano
entries.summary: Combat school based on indirect spells that bypass Magic Resistance; notes aiming with Finesse and the double botch risk of aimed spells.
quotes: indirect spells require two stress rolls (one to cast the spell and another to aim it) and therefore have two chances to botch.

entries.title: Indirect Spells from ArM5
entries.summary: List of core-book spells that can have at least partial effect without penetrating Magic Resistance, with notes on why each works.
quotes: Magic Resistance does not protect against non-magical stone falling due to gravity.
